doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Free jazz, Ascension and avant-garde
summary: He loved those records, did only free improvisation for a time, and values organic, well-played free music.

story.theme_name: Playing with Coltrane and the avant-garde

blocks.x: Lastly, were you familiar with the records “Ascension” and “Free Jazz,” and I wonder what your reaction was to those things at the time.

I loved it. I went through a period where I was doing only free improvisation and my concerts would be just that. And some of those free improvisations would have tonal roots in them and others would be totally pantonal or atonal. So I feel very open to that music, again, it’s a question of how well is it played? How organic does it feel? One of the traps is, as George Russell has been quoted, is that the avante garde is the last refuge of the untalented. Because it’d be very easy for anybody to just pick up a horn and go — —— you know and say hey man, he’s really into it. But how much musical substance?
Right. No rules can be an excuse for a lot of things.
Right. So when that music is well played it’s marvelous, I mean I love it.
